spans.s:
प्र-नष्ट, अस्, आ, अम् (often incorrectly written
प्र-णष्ट), lost, disappeared, vanished, not to be
seen; departed, escaped; perished, destroyed, ruined,
decayed, annihilated.
—प्रनष्ट-ज्ञानिक, अस्, आ,
अम्, ‘whose knowledge is destroyed,’ without know-
ledge.
—प्रनष्ट-विनय, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘whose
politeness has vanished,’ lost to propriety, uncivil,
uncomplaisant, rude.

प्रनष्ट प्र-नष्ट. See under 2. प्र-णश्,
p. 609.

प्रनक्ष् प्र-नक्ष्, cl. 1. P. A. -नक्षति,
-ते, -नक्षितुम्, Ved. to draw near, approach; (Sāy.)
= सर्वतो व्याप्, to be everywhere present.

प्रनर्द् प्र-नर्द्, cl. 1. P. -नर्दति, -नर्दि-
तुम्, see Scholiast on Pāṇ.
VIII. 4, 14

प्रनायक प्र-नायक, अस्, आ, अम्, one whose
leader is away, whose rulers are abroad; destitute of
a guide.

प्रनाल प्र-नाल, प्र-नाली = प्र-णाल, प्र-
णाली, p. 609, col. 3.

प्रनाशिन् प्र-नाशिन्, incorrectly for प्र-
णाशिन्, p. 609, col. 2.

प्रनिंसित प्र-निंसित, प्र-निंसितव्य = प्र-
णिंसित, प्र-णिंसितव्य, p. 609, col. 3.
प्रनिक्षण प्र-निक्षण = प्र-णिक्षण, q. v.

प्रनिघातन प्र-निघातन, अम्, n. (fr. Caus.
of rt. हन् with प्र-नि), killing, slaughter, murder.
प्रनिन्दन प्र-निन्दन = प्र-णिन्दन, q. v.

प्रनिभिद् प्र-नि-भिद्, cl. 7. P. -भिनत्ति,
-भेत्तुम्, see Scholiast on Pāṇ.
VIII. 4, 18

प्रनिरक्ष् प्र-नि-रक्ष्, cl. 1. P. -रक्षति,
-रक्षितुम्, to protect, defend, maintain.

प्रनीड प्र-नीड, अस्, आ, अम्, flown from the
nest, having left a nest.
प्रनुद् प्र-नुद्, incorrectly for प्र-णुद्, q. v.

प्रनृत् प्र-नृत्, cl. 4. P. -नृत्यति, -नर्तितुम्,
to dance forwards, begin to dance, dance; to gesti-
culate as in dancing (in token of derision).

प्र-नर्तित, अस्, आ, अम्, caused to dance forwards,
set in motion, shaken, agitated; dandled.

प्र-नृत्त, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has begun to
dance, dancing; (अम्), n. a dance; (also incorrectly
written प्र-नृत्य.)
—प्रनृत्त-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्,
having danced forward, having begun to dance.

प्र-नृत्यत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, dancing forward,
beginning to dance, dancing.

प्रांशु प्रांशु (प्र-अं˚), उस्, उस्, उ, high,
tall, lofty, of great stature; long; (उस्), m., N. of
a son of Manu Vaivasvata; of a son of Vatsa-prī
(or Vatsa-prīti).
—प्रांशु-ता, f. height, loftiness.
—प्रांशु-लभ्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be obtained or
reached (only) by a tall person.
प्रान् प्रान्. See 1. प्राण्, p. 654, col. 3.

प्रानाडी प्रानाडी, perhaps incorrectly for
प्र-णाडी = प्र-णाली.

प्रान्त प्रान्त (प्र-अन्˚), अस्, अम्, m. n. edge,
margin, verge, border, (ओष्ठ-प्रान्तौ, the corners
of the mouth); boundary, bound, extremity, extreme
verge, end [cf. यौवन-प्˚]; back part; a point,
tip (of a blade of grass); (अस्), m., N. of a man.
—प्रान्त-ग, अस्, आ, अम्, dwelling near the boun-
daries, living close by.
—प्रान्त-तस्, ind. along the
edge or border (of anything), marginally, along or
upon the extremity.
—प्रान्त-दुर्ग, अम्, n. ‘bor-
der-stronghold,’ a suburb or collection of houses
outside the walls of the town, a Petta or town con-
tiguous to a fort and separately fortified.
—प्रान्त-
पुष्पा, f. a kind of plant (having flowers along the
edge of the stem ?).
—प्रान्त-विरस, अस्, आ, अम्,
finally or ultimately insipid, tasteless in the end.
—प्रान्त-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, inhabiting the borders.
प्रान्तायन, अस्, m. a patronymic from Prānta.

प्रान्तर प्रान्तर (प्र-अन्˚), अम्, n. a long
desolate road, a lonesome way or lane, a solitary path;
an intervening long tract of country between two vil-
lages; a forest; the hollow of a tree.
—प्रान्तर-शून्-
य, अम्, n. a long tiresome road (also प्रान्त-शून्य).
